traits.culm_length_m.note: FEIS's narrowleaf cattail review (Snyder 1993, read 2026-10-15): "an erect, rhizomatous perennial that grows 3 to 6 feet (1-2 m) tall"; the flowering stem is the plant's tallest part.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: FEIS's narrowleaf cattail review (Snyder 1993, read 2026-10-15): "Its leaves are 2 to 5 feet (0.6-1.5 m) long, very narrow, and flattened".

traits.leaf_width_m.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives a width; FEIS says only "very narrow".

traits.clonal.note: FEIS's narrowleaf cattail review (Snyder 1993, read 2026-10-15): "once established, colonies are maintained by vegetative reproduction" from lateral rhizomes.

generator.params.note: The cattail program's values, with the leaf and spike lengths the middles of FEIS's ranges (leaves 0.6-1.5 m, fruiting spikes 5-15 cm, Snyder 1993). The organ areas are left to what the looks draw.

allometry.note: 1.5 m at 4 years in the open, the middle of the 1-2 m FEIS gives the plant (Snyder 1993). Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Broadleaf cattail's colours, chosen by eye; the blade drawn as narrow as the stated leaf width allows.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

sources.title: Project After contributors: hand-set species values
sources.licence: project contribution under the repository's terms

provenance.notes: Procedural proxy added with the core-species expansion (2026-10-15): sizes from FEIS, the rest the cattail program's.
